note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a CV 13(1); A06b CV 13(1); L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Cape Verde, 2024
sources.said: Person has been legally resident in Cape Verde for at least 5 years. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Cape Verde to a citizen. ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad and one parent is a citizen in the service of the state; Person is born abroad and one parent is a citizen from birth. ... Parental residence restriction ... Person is born in Cape Verde to parents who have been legally resident for at least 3 years and are not in the service of another state, if person does not declare his or her wish not to be Cape Verdean. ... No provision
